answer: Price new identities on a surge curve: each registration burns a fee that doubles for every hundred sign-ups in the past day, then decays back. Honest agents arrive like a gentle zephyr and pay pennies, but a sybil farm pushing ten thousand fakes through the same inlet drives the fee up a steep knoll, so its last batch costs more than all prior rewards could ever repay. Spreading signups over months to dodge the surge forfeits the early rewards that made the attack worth it.
